reasoning: metric-lammps-cpu is LAMMPS, a real HPC molecular dynamics code. All variants are CPU-only (accelerator none, no gpu_libs), so needs_gpu is false. For a 3-node MPI run the deciding factor is the fabric/MPI stack: the `libfabric-zen4` build is an MPI-only (no OpenMP oversubscription confusion) OpenMPI 4 build layered on an explicitly built libfabric (/opt/libfabric evidence in the sibling reax tag, same lineage), which gives an OFI path that can ride EFA on AWS-style nodes while still falling back to TCP/sockets on plain ethernet — hence network lists both efa and ethernet to OR over rather than pinning a fabric the cluster may not have. Its provenance notes CMAKE_TUNE_FLAGS empty -> generic x86-64, so despite the "zen4" tag name the binary is not ISA-locked and remains portable across amd64 nodes; arch is stamped from the manifest so I do not supply it. This build includes REAXFF, so I use the canonical LAMMPS reaxff/HNS benchmark deck shipped in the image, scaled up with -v x/y/z replication (4x4x2 = 32 unit-cell copies) to give each of the 3 exclusive nodes real work and a meaningful communication surface instead of a trivially small box. Memory: reaxff HNS at this replication is a few GB per node at most, but ReaxFF neighbor/bond lists plus per-rank OpenMPI buffers on a fully-packed exclusive node push well past a tiny 16GB node, so 16-64GB is the safe range without over-reserving into 64-192GB. Node count is exactly the requested 3; cores/ranks are intentionally omitted so the transform derives them from the matched cluster.
